details:
Q1: What should anchor the run list as intake-issued and unmodified?
Choices:
A. Before using any run, check with GraphQL that the heal issue body and each occurrence comment were never edited by anyone except the intake account (via the `lastEditedAt` / `editor` / `userContentEdits` fields). If that can't be shown, ignore all body/comment-supplied runs and the body-derived `source` / `Head SHA` for cross-repo fetches. This costs one batched GraphQL call. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Have the intake also write the run list, source repo, PR and head SHA to a durable record keyed by issue number (on the `ai-memory` branch or a hidden marker written only at creation). The collector trusts only that record. This needs intake + collector changes, and issues filed before the change fall back to issue-repo-only runs.
C. Keep reading runs from the issue prose and rely only on per-run API verification against the body's head SHA / PR. **Note:** this does not close the finding, because those fields are editable too.
Q2: How should cross-repository (consumer) run fetches be authorised?
Choices:
A. Keep `GH_PAT`, but fetch a consumer's runs only when the provenance check (Q1) passes and the run's own API metadata matches the verified repo, head SHA and PR/head branch. Otherwise skip with a logged reason. No new secret. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Add an optional read-only credential limited to a single repo (e.g. a new secret or a GitHub App installation token scoped to the source repo, with a default of unset). When it is unset, skip all consumer-repo run, artifact, timeline and compare fetches; same-repo runs keep `GH_PAT`.
C. Stop cross-repo collection altogether. Only runs in this repository are fetched.
Q3: When some run references fail verification, what should happen to the rest of the evidence folder?
Choices:
A. Skip only the unverifiable runs, record each as a `skipped` entry with its reason in the index, and keep the other sections that already use verified context (provenance, lineage, timeline). (RECOMMENDED)
B. If any run fails verification, drop the whole cross-repo part (runs, timeline, compare) for that issue and keep only same-repo data.
C. Fail the evidence step closed (no folder) whenever any run fails verification. **Note:** this blocks clarify, plan and implement evidence for heal issues with stale or rotated runs.
